description: Change semantics for every module field cluster:lxc owns — the container sibling of cluster:vm.
_note: Read off update-service.sh as it stands. A container is NOT a VM with different words, and the classes differ where the platform does: a container has one NIC, its rootfs is not grown in place by this service, and it is not live-migrated at all — an LXC with a GPU or a bind-mount cannot be moved safely, so `node` is a manual operation rather than cluster:vm's `migrate`. Where cluster:vm auto-applies, this warns; those fields are classed `manual`, which is exactly what 'reported, never applied silently' means.

vmname.changeNote: Proxmox calls a container's name 'hostname'. It is also the DNS name the guest registers as.

vmtag.changeNote: Same canonicalisation and same rule as cluster:vm: the schema default 'TAPPaaS' is desired state, and it is what Create-TAPPaaS-LXC.sh applies when the module declares nothing, so an undeclared container is already in sync.

cores.changeNote: Applied live — a container's cgroup limit changes without a restart.

coresMinMax.changeNote: A sizing policy (ADR-044), read when the config is written: at install and before the 3-way merge on update, where it picks the value of the field it sizes for the site's or environment's size. Nothing on the cluster to compare.

memory.changeNote: Also live, for the same reason.

memoryMinMax.changeNote: A sizing policy (ADR-044), read when the config is written: at install and before the 3-way merge on update, where it picks the value of the field it sizes for the site's or environment's size. Nothing on the cluster to compare.

swap.description: Swap in MB for an LXC container. A container has no BIOS and no virtual disk controller, so its memory pressure is handled differently from a VM's — 0 means the container may not swap at all, which is the TAPPaaS default.
swap.note: cluster:lxc's update-service.sh has always read this from config with a default of 0; it was simply never declared here, so no path could report or classify it.
swap.changeNote: Container-only: a VM's swap is inside its guest, a container's is a host-side cgroup limit. Live, like cores and memory. TAPPaaS defaults it to 0 — a container that needs swap says so.

bridge0.changeNote: A bridge change moves the container to a different L2 segment, so it must re-DHCP — hence the restart.

zone0.changeNote: The zone resolves to net0's VLAN tag; a new tag is a new subnet, so the container restarts and re-registers DNS.

mac0.changeNote: Spelled `hwaddr=` on a container, and the same reasoning as cluster:vm's mac0: a new MAC is a new lease, and under masqdns the container's name follows that lease — so the restart and the stale-pin cleanup both matter. Preserved from the live NIC unless the module pins one, which is why both reporters emit the MAC under one key.

trunks0.changeNote: A trunk-only change applies live on the bridge — no restart.

node.changeNote: NOT cluster:vm's `migrate`. Live-migrating a container is unsafe when it has a GPU passed through or bind-mounts from the host — which is why TAPPaaS runs containers for exactly those workloads. The service reports the drift and leaves the move to an operator who can stop it, move it and start it deliberately.

diskSize.changeNote: The rootfs grows live with pct resize (update-disk.sh), and auto-grow.sh grows it before it fills, as for a VM: on every update, under the same threshold, diskSizeMax and pool limits. A SHRINK is refused at apply time (hook exit 20). Only the rootfs is the field; bind mounts and other mount points are never resized. The schema default 8G is what Create-TAPPaaS-LXC.sh builds with, so an undeclared container is in sync from install; a rootfs grown by hand reads as config behind actual and is adopted into config, as for cluster:vm.

diskMinMax.changeNote: A sizing policy (ADR-044), read when the config is written: at install and before the 3-way merge on update, where it picks the value of the field it sizes for the site's or environment's size. Nothing on the cluster to compare.

storage.changeNote: As cluster:vm, and for a bind-mounted container this is not a move at all. The schema default 'tanka1' is what Create-TAPPaaS-LXC.sh builds on, so an undeclared container is in sync from install and the manual-class report is restored rather than suppressed (ADR-020 D9).

vmid.changeNote: The container's identity. A different vmid IS a different container.

image.changeNote: The template the container was created from.

imageType.changeNote: How it was built; not re-decidable in place.

net0.changeNote: The container's only NIC — TAPPaaS gives a CT one interface, which is why bridge1/mac1/zone1/trunks1 are cluster:vm-only. Proxmox spells it 'name=eth0,bridge=…,hwaddr=…,ip=dhcp[,tag=…]'. in-place-reboot is the CEILING: a MAC- or trunk-only change stays in-place, and only a bridge/zone change restarts the container.
